# Why therapy practices are leaving their EHR (and 6 questions to ask before switching)

Rising costs and rushed features have therapy practices reconsidering their EHR. See what to look for, and 6 questions to ask before switching.

Melissa Bhatia

Published on Jul 22, 2026

Updated on Jul 22, 2026

As a clinician, your number one focus is your clients, not your software. That instinct is understandable. But when you're running a private practice, you're also a business owner, and that means looking at the tools your practice depends on with a different lens. Familiarity is comfortable, but it isn't the same as being a good long-term decision.

That's where an honest evaluation begins: not with whether the EHR still works, but with whether price has kept pace with the product. It's a pattern many practice owners are noticing: EHR costs climbing steadily, sometimes sharply, while the underlying product doesn't show the same rate of improvement. And when new features drop, AI included, they don't always feel like the result of careful work. Some are switched on by default, with little explanation of what happens to the data behind them. For some business owners, that combination is the catalyst to start looking at alternative platforms, and to be very intentional on what they are looking for before making the change.

# SimplePractice Reviews: What Practices Actually Say in 2026

The verdict depends almost entirely on your size

Jana Hindiyeh· April 21, 2026· 6 min read

## Key takeaways

- Solo therapists rate SimplePractice highly and are broadly right to.
- Complaints cluster tightly around what happens as a practice grows.
- Forced supervisor sign-off regardless of credential status is the most specific gap.
- Interns cost the same as fully licensed clinicians.
- There is no API, so analytics and attribution cannot be connected.

Short answer: SimplePractice is genuinely well built and most solo therapists who use it are happy with it. The complaints cluster almost entirely around one thing, what happens when a practice grows. Supervision, permissions, intern pricing, couples records, and billing at volume are where the reviews turn negative, and they turn negative in the same places across practice after practice.

# The $20,000 "Hidden Tax" Quietly Bankrupting Solo Therapists

Why recurring EHR subscription costs create financial burnout for solo therapists, and how the long-term math can quietly erase tens of thousands in profit.

We talk a lot about burnout in this field. Compassion fatigue. Setting boundaries. The heavy emotional toll of just showing up and holding space for people day after day. It is a lot.

But you know what almost nobody brings up? Financial burnout.

You did not leave an agency job just to trade one demanding boss for a giant pile of monthly software receipts. You made the leap for freedom. You wanted to call the shots with your schedule, your caseload, and your bank account. Yet, give it a few months, and you will likely realize your profit margins are bleeding out.

The biggest parasite draining your bank account? Your Electronic Health Record (EHR) system.
